Mina — thanks for the heads-up and congrats on the product launch plans. We can absolutely support a few different approaches; below are three pragmatic paths so your finance and infra teams can weigh trade-offs quickly. I'll also propose a 30-minute alignment call if helpful.

Option A — Accelerated commit (preferred for lowest unit cost)
- Increase reserved commit by 50% for 12 months
- 10-12% unit discount on committed usage
- One-time implementation credit to offset ramping costs (suggested: $40k)
- Standard true-up at year-end

Option B — Staged commit + short-term price hold (min friction)
- Initial 3-month price hold at current rates while you ramp
- 90-day staged commit increase (we mirror observed ramp-weekly usage into commit)
- Smaller upfront credit ($20k) to offset spike risk

Option C — Conservative commit + credits
- Keep current commit, provide burst buffer and a larger credit for unexpected overages (e.g., $60k credit)
- No discount on committed units

Quick ask: can you share last 3 months of usage by model (or let us analyze if you send usage CSV)? I want to run the numbers with Product and Finance to confirm margin impact.

If these look reasonable I can loop in Finance for a formal pricing sheet.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec — North America
Redwood Inference

Jordan — high level thoughts:

- Offer structure I'd recommend: 40% committed bump (12-month term) + 8% committed unit discount, with a 3-month onboarding price hold at current invoice rate (no discount during hold). After month 3 we transition to committed pricing.
- Add a $35k implementation/onboarding credit applied against the first invoice to smooth their cash flow.
- To protect margin, set a burst cap of 2.5x baseline (we can bill excess at overage rates after third month) and include a clause to revisit if sustained over 60%.

Agree with Lauren but prefer to shift some of the concession into credits rather than lowering unit price too far. Margin math: 8% discount + $35k credit approximates to a slightly larger revenue impact than a 6% discount + $50k credit for Year 1.

Counter-suggested final:
- 6% committed discount on the bumped commit (12 months)
- $50k implementation/onboarding credit (applied over first two invoices)
- 3-month price hold at current invoice rates; after month 3, committed rates apply
- Clear true-up at month 12 and right to renegotiate if usage > 150% of new commit for 2 consecutive months

That keeps our blended unit economics healthier while giving NovaGrid the runway.

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts

Proposal (commercial summary)
- Commit: 50% increase to reserved capacity for 12 months (effective at renewal start)
- Pricing: 6% committed discount on the bumped commit (Year 1)
- Credits: $50,000 implementation/onboarding credit applied across first two invoices
- Price hold: 90-day hold at your current invoice rate (no discount applied during the hold). After 90 days rates move to the committed pricing above.
- Risk protection: burst cap at 2.5x baseline for months 0-3; overages billed at standard overage rates. True-up at month 12; if usage >150% of new commit for 2 consecutive months, we reserve the right to reopen economics.

Attachments included:
- Renewal_Proposal_NovaGrid_Q3-2026.pdf (proposal with line-item pricing and SOW summary)

3) Implementation plan kick-off within two weeks of signature.
